item.name: Auth
item.description:
JWT authentication endpoints.

User accounts are not created through the API. To create a user:
• Django admin UI: http://localhost:8000/admin/
• Management command: python manage.py createsuperuser

Once a user exists, obtain a token pair with POST /auth/token/ and include the access token as a Bearer token on all subsequent requests. Access tokens expire — use POST /auth/token/refresh/ with the refresh token to get a new one without re-entering credentials.

request.description: Flip the per-environment kill switch (EnvironmentFlag.is_enabled) for the named environment. The state is created on first toggle (off by default), invalidates the flag cache, and writes an audit entry.

operator choices: eq, neq, contains, in, not_in, gt, lt

serve_variation: null for boolean flags (returns true on match). For multivariate flags, set to a variation ID to serve a specific variation when this rule matches.

response.name: 400 Bad Request — Flag not found or not accessible

request.description: Users matching this rule are served variation ID 3. Use for multivariate targeting — e.g. premium users get the 'red' button, free users get 'blue'.

request.description:
key_type choices: server, client.

The full key is returned once in the `key` field and auto-saved to {{sdk_key}}. Store it — it cannot be recovered after this response.

request.description: Revokes the old key and issues a replacement. The new full key is auto-saved to {{sdk_key}}.

response.name: 201 Created — New key issued, old key revoked

request.description:
Auth: X-SDK-Key header. Set {{sdk_key}} via Create SDK Key or Rotate SDK Key — the test script auto-saves it.

Response:
{
  "flag_key": "dark-mode",
  "result": true,
  "result_type": "boolean",
  "environment": "production"
}

result_type values: boolean | string | number | json
For multivariate flags, result is the variation value (e.g. "red", 5000, {"color": "#f00"}).
